newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday July 29.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Prime minister Romano Prodi is expected to meet union representatives and employers on Tuesday to end first-round talks on welfare state reform before the summer break (all).

* The lira fell to 12-year low against the U.S. dollar at over 1,800 (all). Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said the dollar's rise did not mean Italian consumer price inflation would start to pick up. Ciampi also said he did not see tensions on interest rates (La Repubblica).

* Gian Maria Gros Pietro, chairman of state industrial holding IRI, said in an interview that flag carrier Alitalia, due to be privatised in two years, would find the economic ally it has been looking for by the end of the year. Gros Pietro also said IRI's new board in September would have to deal with the sale of railroad group Autostrade and the re engineering group of Finmeccanica (Sole 24 Ore/La Repubblica).
* The charitable foundation that owns savings bank Cariplo said it had given its formal approval to the planned merger with Banco Ambrosiano Veneto (all).
* Sergio Cragnotti, chairman of food processing firm Cirio Spa, said the group comprising Cirio and Brazil's Bombril currently had debts totalling 825 billion lire (all).
